name: Editing Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building editing — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary editing tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building editing — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary editing tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that editing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. When multiple editing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Validate editing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
4. When editing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. When editing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to editing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Keep editing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. Prefer explicit, readable editing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. Measure before optimizing any editing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
10. Prefer the simplest editing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
11. Surface known limitations of a chosen editing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
12. Keep editing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new editing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated editing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting editing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about editing over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
